in-need-of-your-skills.text: Eluned hands you a tiny crystal seed.

in-need-of-your-skills.speaker: Eluned
in-need-of-your-skills.text: Here you go... If you ever need to get back to Lletya, you can use this.

in-need-of-your-skills.speaker: Eluned
in-need-of-your-skills.text: Use it sparingly as it only has a few uses. If you need, I can re-enchant it, but I am not as talented as the singer who originally made this one.

in-need-of-your-skills.speaker: Eluned
in-need-of-your-skills.text: Now, I had better get going or Islwyn will get worried.

in-need-of-your-skills.speaker: Arianwyn
in-need-of-your-skills.text: Ah [player name], glad to see you made it. Welcome to Lletya, home to the Elven Resistance.

in-need-of-your-skills.player: Thank you. It wasn't particularly easy to get here, it took some work to convince Islwyn I could be trusted.

in-need-of-your-skills.speaker: Arianwyn
in-need-of-your-skills.text: That's not surprising, he is not particularly fond of humans. But if you've earnt his trust, it proves to me that I was right to take a chance on you.

in-need-of-your-skills.player: I'm glad you did. I hate the thought that I might still be blindly working for King Lathas and Lord Iorwerth right now.

in-need-of-your-skills.speaker: Arianwyn
in-need-of-your-skills.text: Well you're here now and you still have a chance to right your previous wrongs.

in-need-of-your-skills.player: I hope so. There's a lot I still don't understand though. Why are King Lathas and Lord Iorwerth working together? Where does the plague fit in?

in-need-of-your-skills.speaker: Arianwyn
in-need-of-your-skills.text: I'm afraid that a lot is still unknown to us as well. However, I will explain what I can. Be aware that this is only a brief overview. You'll find some books around the village that explain more if you wish though.

options.text: Okay, let's begin

steps.player: Okay, let's begin.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: Many years ago, all elves lived in harmony within the crystal city of Prifddinas alongside our goddess, Seren.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: When the God Wars ended, Seren was lost to us. For the first time, we were alone. To lead us through those difficult times, Baxtorian Cadarn was named the first king of the elves.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: Under Baxtorian, our kingdom expanded into the east. We prospered for a time, but little did we know that an enemy walked among us.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: During that time, Lord Iorwerth turned away from Seren and pledged himself to Zamorak, the Dark Lord.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: A larger kingdom meant our forces were further spread. Lord Iorwerth took advantage of that. He claimed Prifddinas as his own.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: Baxtorian tried to take it back from him, but Prifddinas was built to survive the God Wars. There was no way to retake it.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: In a last attempt to keep the city safe, Baxtorian and the clan elders sung the song of inversion which reverted the entire city into a crystal seed.

steps.player: Ah, so that explains why the city just looks like an empty field.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: Indeed. After that, Baxtorian returned to the east but found that the rest of the kingdom had fallen while he was away. Not only that, but his wife, Glarial, had been taken.

steps.player: I know this bit, Baxtorian retreated into his home beneath the waterfall and never came out. I moved Glarial's remains into the waterfall so they could be together.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: That's good to hear, I can see why you managed to earn Islwyn's trust.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: Anyway, with Baxtorian gone and Prifddinas lost, our land erupted into a Civil War. We've been fighting ever since.

steps.player: I see, it's good to have a bit more understanding. But where does King Lathas come into this?

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: That is the bit we're not so sure on. We know little about the lands to the east. From what we can tell, it seems that Lord Iorwerth has promised to support King Lathas in reclaiming some land his family once owned.

steps.player: But why? What's in it for Lord Iorwerth.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: That's what we want you to find out. According to our spies, Lord Iorwerth has used the alliance with King Lathas as an opportunity to infiltrate West Ardougne. The city must contain something he needs.

steps.player: Infiltrate? How?

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: Those that you know as mourners are in fact elves in service to Lord Iorwerth. We regularly see them crossing the Arandar mountain pass and into the east.

steps.player: Mourners are elves?

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: That they are. We assume that the plague is a cover up for them to enter the city unchallenged. We don't know why though. That's why we need you.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: You know the city and can freely travel there. You are the perfect person for this task. We need you to go to West Ardougne, infiltrate the mourners and find out what they are doing in the city.

options.text: Let's skip the backstory.

steps.player: Let's skip the backstory.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: I'd argue that understanding is essential to what comes next. But as you wish.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: The bit that is relevant to you is the recent alliance between King Lathas and Lord Iorwerth.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: From what we can tell, it seems that Lord Iorwerth has promised to support King Lathas in reclaiming some land his family once owned.

steps.player: But why? What's in it for Lord Iorwerth.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: That's what we want you to find out. According to our spies, Lord Iorwerth has used the alliance with King Lathas as an opportunity to infiltrate West Ardougne. The city must contain something he needs.

steps.player: Infiltrate? How?

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: Those that you know as mourners are in fact elves in service to Lord Iorwerth. We regularly see them crossing the Arandar mountain pass and into the east.

steps.player: Mourners are elves?

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: That they are. We assume that the plague is a cover up for them to enter the city unchallenged. We don't know why though. That's why we need you.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: You know the city and can freely travel there. You are the perfect person for this task. We need you to go to West Ardougne, infiltrate the mourners and find out what they are doing in the city.

in-need-of-your-skills.player: So you want me to infiltrate the mourners? How am I supposed to achieve that?

in-need-of-your-skills.speaker: Arianwyn
in-need-of-your-skills.text: I don't have an exact plan for you I'm afraid. You know the city better than any of us so are best placed to make a plan yourself.

in-need-of-your-skills.speaker: Arianwyn
in-need-of-your-skills.text: However as I said before, there have been sightings of mourners crossing the Arandar mountain pass. I'm sure you can take advantage of that.

in-need-of-your-skills.player: Alright, I'll see what I can do.

the-mourner-s-disguise-attacking-a-mourn.speaker: Mourner
the-mourner-s-disguise-attacking-a-mourn.text: This will cut down you to size!

the-mourner-s-disguise-asking-arianwyn-f.player: I killed one of those mourners crossing the mountain pass and took their clothes.
I do have a bit of an issue though. The top has blood on it and the trousers are ripped.

the-mourner-s-disguise-asking-arianwyn-f.speaker: Arianwyn
the-mourner-s-disguise-asking-arianwyn-f.text: Hmm... Well you can try asking our local seamstress, Oronwen, about the trousers.

the-mourner-s-disguise-asking-arianwyn-f.speaker: Arianwyn
the-mourner-s-disguise-asking-arianwyn-f.text: As for the top, you'll need to find a way to get it cleaned. Maybe you can find someone who does a lot of laundry. Someone who wears lots of white might be a good bet.

the-mourner-s-disguise-using-the-bloody-.text: Just wetting the top will not remove the bloodstains.

options.text: Many greetings.
I seek knowledge and power!
Could you wash this top for me?

steps.player: Could you wash this top for me?

steps.speaker: Seer
steps.text: And why would I do that?

steps.player: Well with how white your robes are, I assumed that you'd know a thing or two about keeping clothes clean.

steps.speaker: Seer
steps.text: Oh no, we outsource all of that to those Druids in Taverley. Cheaper and quicker than doing it ourselves.

steps.player: I see. Thanks for the help.

the-mourner-s-disguise-talking-to-tegid.speaker: Tegid
the-mourner-s-disguise-talking-to-tegid.text: Yes. What is it to you?

the-mourner-s-disguise-talking-to-tegid.player: Do you know any way to remove blood stains?

the-mourner-s-disguise-talking-to-tegid.speaker: Tegid
the-mourner-s-disguise-talking-to-tegid.text: Blood stains is it... Well, the soap I use can clean almost any stain.

the-mourner-s-disguise-talking-to-tegid.player: Really?!? That sounds like just the thing I need, can I use some?

the-mourner-s-disguise-talking-to-tegid.speaker: Tegid
the-mourner-s-disguise-talking-to-tegid.text: No, I don't have very much soap left and I still have lots to get clean.

the-mourner-s-disguise-talking-to-tegid.player: Alright can you tell me where I can buy some?

the-mourner-s-disguise-talking-to-tegid.speaker: Tegid
the-mourner-s-disguise-talking-to-tegid.text: You can't... I make it to my own secret recipe.
If Eadgar's Ruse has been completed:

steps.player: Could you be less helpful?

steps.speaker: Tegid
steps.text: Like you were, taking those robes from my washing line?? So yes, if you know a way I can be less helpful just tell me. I'll try it.

the-mourner-s-disguise-stealing-from-the.text: You search the laundry basket... It's full of dirty robes.
You search the laundry basket... It's full of dirty robes, On top you see a bar of soap.

options.text: Steal the soap.

steps.text: If the inventory is full:
You don't have enough room to take the soap.
You wait until Tegid is looking the other way... and steal the soap!

options.text: Leave the soap.

steps.text: You leave the soap where it is.

the-mourner-s-disguise-use-tegid-s-soap-.text: The dry soap has no effect.
You give the top a good scrub with the soap and rinse away the bloody suds with water.

the-mourner-s-disguise-trousers.speaker: Oronwen
the-mourner-s-disguise-trousers.text: I do, but human clothes are too hard to mend. They do not have the finesse of elven garments.

the-mourner-s-disguise-trousers.player: I need you to repair some elven clothing as it goes.

the-mourner-s-disguise-trousers.speaker: Oronwen
the-mourner-s-disguise-trousers.text: Let me take a look at it then.
You show the seamstress the mourner trousers.

the-mourner-s-disguise-trousers.speaker: Oronwen
the-mourner-s-disguise-trousers.text: There's something disturbingly familiar about the design of these trousers, they are made for an elf.

the-mourner-s-disguise-trousers.speaker: Oronwen
the-mourner-s-disguise-trousers.text: Of course I can, but I will need two pieces of silk and some bear fur.
If the player already has the required items on them:

steps.player: Great, I have those here.

steps.speaker: Oronwen
steps.text: Huh, it's almost like you knew what I needed.
Oronwen hands you the mourner trousers, they look as good as new.

steps.player: Thanks a lot.

steps.speaker: Oronwen
steps.text: Any time.

options.text: Yes please. What are you selling?
No thanks.
What do you need to mend my trousers?

steps.player: What do you need to mend my trousers?

steps.speaker: Oronwen
steps.text: I need bear fur and two pieces of silk.

steps.player: Alright.

options.text: Yes please. What are you selling?
No thanks.
I have all I need to mend my trousers.

steps.player: I have all I need to mend my trousers.

steps.speaker: Oronwen
steps.text: Pass it all here then, and I will get started.
Oronwen hands you the mourner trousers, they look as good as new.

steps.player: Thanks a lot.

steps.speaker: Oronwen
steps.text: Any time.

the-mourner-s-disguise-trousers-talking-.text: You give the silk to Oronwen.
If more silk and bear fur is needed:

steps.speaker: Oronwen
steps.text: I need bear fur and one piece of silk.

the-mourner-s-disguise-trousers-talking-.text: If only bear fur is needed:

steps.speaker: Oronwen
steps.text: I only need bear fur now.

steps.speaker: Oronwen
steps.text: I need two pieces of silk.

steps.speaker: Oronwen
steps.text: I only need one piece of silk.

the-mourner-s-disguise-reporting-to-aria.player: I killed one of those mourners crossing the mountain pass and took their clothes.

the-mourner-s-disguise-reporting-to-aria.speaker: Arianwyn
the-mourner-s-disguise-reporting-to-aria.text: Ah, a disguise. Good thinking. Use it to enter the Mourner Headquarters in West Ardougne. Once your in, see if you can find out what they are doing in the city.

earning-their-trust-inside-the-headquart.speaker: Mourner
earning-their-trust-inside-the-headquart.text: It is good to see so many new recruits, soon no one will be able to stand against the power of the Death Guard.

earning-their-trust-inside-the-headquart.speaker: Mourner
earning-their-trust-inside-the-headquart.text: Indeed it is. You should speak with Essyllt downstairs. He's in charge.

options.text: Dialogue 1:

steps.player: Hello.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: Good day. Are you in need of assistance?

options.text: Dialogue 2:

steps.player: Good day.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: Are the townspeople causing you trouble?

options.text: Yes, but I don't think you can help

steps.player: Yes, but I don't think you can help

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: You will be surprised at how much help the brute force of the Guard can be.

steps.player: Well I'll be sure to ask if I'm in need of some muscle.

options.text: No, I just wanted to talk to a friendly face.

steps.player: No, I just wanted to talk to a friendly face.

steps.speaker: Mourner
steps.text: Do I look friendly to you? I really must work on my scowl more.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Ah... I take it you are one of the new recruits?

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: I'm Essyllt and I'm in charge here. Now come on, let us have a look at your paper work.
You hand over the letter of recommendation.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: This seems to be all in order. Welcome to the Death Guard. Now, for your first assignment...

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: As you may know, part of what we do here is keep the people believing in the plague...

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Did they not tell you? Hmm... I'd better fill you in.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Well as you undoubtedly know, we were sent here by Lord Iorwerth to secure the city. The reason for this is so that we can access the caves below...

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: I'm afraid that information is classified until you prove your commitment to the Death Guard.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Now to keep our presence in the city secret, Lord Iorwerth arranged an alliance with King Lathas, the ruler in the east.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Apparently the fool thinks we will help him dispose of the Knights of Camelot once our work here is done. I expect he'll be disappointed.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Anyway, the plague serves two purposes. First, it allows us to move around the city in secret thanks to our mourner disguises.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Second, it means we can abduct citizens to mine the caves below with ease. We just pretend they've fallen victim to the plague.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Well we have had a few near misses. Recently we had some girl from East Ardougne poking around asking too many questions, so we locked her up while we decided what to do with her.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Annoyingly, she managed to escape with the help of some adventurer. Lucky for us, they were so stupid that we managed to use the adventurer to deal with King Tyras. It all worked out quite well in the end.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Things like that is why we must ensure the people keep believing in the plague though. One of the things we do to keep up the lie is to fool old Farmer Brumty into believing his sheep are infected.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: The old halfwit thinks just because his sheep are an abnormal colour, that they are all ill with plague. It's amazing what a bit of dye can do.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Well you don't think they end up those ridiculous colours naturally do you?

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Anyway, shame of it is that we have yet to find a way to stop the dye from washing out. So we need someone, that someone being you, to go and re-dye them.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.player: Simple enough, you want me to give a blue rinse to a load of old sheep?

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Not quite, for starters the sheep need to be dyed red, yellow, green and blue. But most important is that you are not seen doing this by anyone.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Also you will need to re-dye them the colours they already are or the farmer may notice the change.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.player: That sounds a little more tricky. How did you do it before?

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: We have a gnomic device that fires fat dye parcels that rupture on impact.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Unfortunately, we have run out of the parcels and the device is broken.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.player: Can I take a look at it?

earning-their-trust-new-recruit.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit.text: Sure. We have a gnome inventor here too. Sadly, he is not being very helpful about fixing it, but you can talk to him if you like. Here is the key, he is in the next room. And here's the device as well.
Essyllt hands you a strange object and a tarnished key.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit-lost-ite.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-new-recruit-lost-ite.text: Have you finished with those sheep yet?
If the player has lost both the broken device and tarnished key:

steps.player: No, I'm sorry I lost the gnomic device and the key.

steps.speaker: Essyllt
steps.text: Well it is lucky we have a whole stack of broken devices, there must be some flaw in the design, they always break in the same way. If you ever need another there is a chest full of them over there.

steps.speaker: Essyllt
steps.text: I also keep copies of the key on my desk so I can replace that too.
Essyllt hands you a strange object and a tarnished key.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit-lost-ite.text: If the player has lost the broken device:

steps.player: Not yet, I lost the gnomic device.

steps.speaker: Essyllt
steps.text: Well it is lucky we have a whole stack of broken ones, there must be some flaw in the design, they always break in the same way. If you ever need another there is a chest full of them over there.

earning-their-trust-new-recruit-lost-ite.text: Essyllt hands you a strange object.

steps.text: If the player has lost the tarnished key:

steps.player: I'm sorry but I lost the key.

steps.speaker: Essyllt
steps.text: I keep copies of the key on my desk so I can replace that.
Essyllt hands you a tarnished key.

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.player: Hello, will you help me fix this... err... thing?

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.speaker: Gnome on a rack
earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.text: I'm not helping you fix that, as if it hasn't caused enough trouble as it is. Your friends have already tried every torture in the book!

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.speaker: Gnome on a rack
earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.text: I'm still not telling anyone squat.

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.player: Have they tried... err... Stretching your eyelids yet?
How about... feeding you nail and prune stew?

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.speaker: Gnome on a rack
earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.text: That's all I've been living on since I got here.

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.player: Set fire to your nostril hair? Let rabid rabbits nibble your toes? Given you a twisted arm?

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.speaker: Gnome on a rack
earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.text: Yes, yes and yes. Tried them all, quite liked the toe nibbling.

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.speaker: Gnome on a rack
earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.text: Us gnomes aren't wise so we don't get them. Face it, you'll never put me in enough pain that I'll tell you what you wanna know.

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.speaker: Gnome on a rack
earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.text: I used to play gnomeball as a kid. This is a walk in the park in comparison.

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.player: Alright I get the picture. What will work then?

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.speaker: Gnome on a rack
earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.text: Ha! You think I'm stupid enough to tell you that I've been craving toad crunchies or that I can't stand having my feet tickled!

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.player: Err... But you just told me?!?

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.speaker: Gnome on a rack
earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-barg.text: I did? What did I say?

options.text: You said about going to the park and playing gnomeball.

steps.player: You said about going to the park and playing gnomeball.

steps.speaker: Gnome on a rack
steps.text: Yes yes!! That was it, I'd hate that. Please don't do that. By Guthix's beard you mourners are such idiots!

steps.speaker: Gnome on a rack
steps.text: Leave me be moron.

options.text: You said about toad crunchies and a gnome ball.

steps.player: You said about toad crunchies and a gnome ball.

steps.speaker: Gnome on a rack
steps.text: I used to play gnomeball yes... what's that got to do with anything? Nothing that can convince me to help you that's for sure.

steps.speaker: Gnome on a rack
steps.text: Go away imbecile.

options.text: You said about toad crunchies and being tickled.

steps.player: You said about toad crunchies and being tickled.

steps.speaker: Gnome on a rack
steps.text: Oops... I mean erm... No that must have been some other err... gnome...

steps.player: You're not fooling me... So you'll help me in exchange for toad crunchies?

steps.speaker: Gnome on a rack
steps.text: If you think you can just buy my co-operation you're a bigger imbecile than I thought.

steps.player: You will tell me, sooner or later.

options.text: You said about being tickled and a gnome ball.

steps.player: You said about being tickled and a gnome ball.

steps.speaker: Gnome on a rack
steps.text: Oooh... a big scary gnomeball. I mean, it might crush me and my entire family, because we're so small!

steps.speaker: Gnome on a rack
steps.text: They have big teeth and everything don't they? Sheesh. You mourners will have to try better than that. Now go away. I need some sleep after all these *yawn* scary threats.

options.text: You said about being tickled and going to the park.

steps.player: You said about being tickled and going to the park.

steps.speaker: Gnome on a rack
steps.text: No... I said being here is a walk in the park. Where do they get you guys? You must all be ogre rejects for being too thick.

steps.speaker: Gnome on a rack
steps.text: Leave me be idiot.

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-talk.speaker: Gnome on a rack
earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-talk.text: I've got nothing to say to you!

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-with.text: You dangle the toad crunchie above the gnome's nose.
The gnome cranes his neck and gulps down the toad crunchie before you can pull them away.

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-with.speaker: Gnome on a rack
earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-with.text: I told you you can't buy my cooperation...

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-tick.text: You dangle the toad crunchie above the gnome's nose just out of reach and hold the feather menacingly close to his feet.

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-tick.player: Now will you help me or would you prefer it if I tickle your feet?

earning-their-trust-torture-chamber-tick.speaker: Gnome on a rack

earning-their-trust-speaking-to-elena.speaker: Elena

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Yes, it is done. What next?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: It is good to see your enthusiasm. I was going to get one of the others to do this job, but as you are here...

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: It has been quite some time since anyone got ill from the plague, so I would like you to see to it that people do!

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Err... But the plague doesn't exist, how am I meant to do that?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: We have never tried this before, but some joker put something in our food not too long ago that gave us all symptoms akin to those of the plague.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: If you can find out what it was that we were poisoned with, you could reproduce the effects. If done right the poison should not be fatal and could help restock our dwindling supply of cheap labour.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: We can have our men remove the 'infected' citizens and sent into the mines.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: Distribution should be easy enough. Because of the city walls no one can grow their own food. Instead, all the food here comes from one of three supply points.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Let me get this clear, you want me to find out who poisoned you, find out what they poisoned you with, find out how to make the poison and produce enough poison to affect a lot of people?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: Don't forget the part where you use the poison to contaminate the food supply. Two of the three supply points should be enough.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: How am I meant to do all of that?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: You seem resourceful so I'm sure you will come up with something. I would help you but I am not a biologist.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Luckily for me I know a biologist nearby.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: Someone trustworthy I hope?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Oh yes, definitely.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: Very well. Perform this task and then return to me.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Essyllt

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Essyllt
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: Subtle as a brick... Yes that, how is it going?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Can you explain to me again what it is I have to do?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Essyllt

steps.text: Well I'm not going anywhere.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Well I'll start from when we found out that the plague was a hoax. When I confronted the king, he told me that he faked the plague to keep people safe from his brother, King Tyras.
He said that Tyras was taken by the Dark Lord while exploring the lands to the west. He claimed that the Dark Lord corrupted him by forcing him to drink from the Chalice of Eternity.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: But that was a lie?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Indeed, but I didn't find out until much later. On the kings orders, I travelled through the Underground Pass and into the western lands of Tirannwn.
Once there, I met up with Lord Iorwerth, the leader of some elves that had allied with the king. He helped me kill King Tyras.
That was when I discovered the truth. While returning to King Lathas, I was confronted by another elf named Arianwyn, the leader of a group of rebel elves opposing Lord Iorwerth.
At the time, I was carrying a letter from Lord Iorwerth to King Lathas. Arianwyn magically broke the seal on the letter so I could read it.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: What did it say?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: It revealed that it's actually King Lathas and Lord Iorwerth who serve the Dark Lord. According to the letter, King Lathas wants to reclaim Camelot from King Arthur and believes the Dark Lord can help him.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: And Lord Iorwerth?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: I'm not exactly sure yet. West Ardougne seems to be key to his plans though. I met with Arianwyn who revealed to me that the mourners are actually elves in service to Lord Iorwerth.
I've infiltrated the mourners and I'm trying to work out what they are doing. From what I've learnt so far, there's something important to them in the caves below West Ardougne.
I'm currently working with them to earn their trust. Hopefully they'll reveal their plans to me soon.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: I see, that's quite the reveal. If you need anything from me just ask.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Well, I was hoping you could help me with something.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: What's the problem?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: I've been asked to produce a poison based on rotten apples.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: I doubt any poison based solely on apples, rotten or not, would be very effective.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Well I put a rotten apple in the mourners' stew, I'm told that the effect was much like the symptoms of the plague.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: Hmm... That sounds like they were ill from some sort of toxin, I should think it was a mould of some sort that had the effect, not the rotten apple itself. What do you need it for?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: I need to poison a large food supply in order to get the mourners' trust.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: That's awful, I can't help you with that.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: If I don't gain the trust of the mourners, then the people of West Ardougne will have a much worse time than the effects of that toxin. Elena trust me.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: You'd better be right about this, and I'd better make sure you get this toxin right so no one dies!

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: Bring me a sample of rotten apple to examine. I'll also see if I can make a counteractant for the toxin.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: How big is the store that you're going to affect?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Well I was instructed to contaminate two of the three supply points in West Ardougne.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: That's over half of the food in the city! You're going to need a huge amount of the toxin to do that. You're also going to need to refine it too, or people will notice rotten apples in amongst the food.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: This is starting to sound a little tricky, can't you make it for me?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: I would, but I don't have the right equipment here to do anything in bulk.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Alright then, tell me the process and I'll get started.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: Right then, the first thing to do is mash up a lot of rotten apples, then you will need to dissolve the toxin into a liquid that has a very low evaporation point, some form of solvent.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: I don't know as much about those kinds of chemicals but I believe naphtha will be perfect for this.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Ah yes, I've worked with naphtha before. The chemist in Rimmington helped me make it from coal tar.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: Perfect. Well get yourself some naphtha and some mashed rotten apples and mix them together. Once you've done that, strain out any solids.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: Finally, heat the mixture to evaporate off the solvent. Be careful of naked flames as the solvent will be highly flammable.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: And that's all is it? Why isn't anything ever easy?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: Sorry, I never said it would be simple. Here, you'll need this to strain out the solids.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: You may want to check out the orchard just north of the city. I hear no one has tended it since the blight infected the trees there. I imagine it will have plenty of rotten apples.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: It will take forever to fill like this. I need something that can transport lots of rotten apples in it.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Not too well, can you remind me how I should make it again?

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: Next, you'll want to get yourself some naphtha and mix it with the rotten apples. You mentioned the chemist in Rimmingon helped you with naphtha before. You might want to speak to him again.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: Once that's done, use the sieve I gave you to strain out any solids. Finally, heat the mixture to evaporate off the solvent. Be careful of naked flames as the solvent will be highly flammable.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.player: Okay, thanks Elena.

earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.speaker: Elena
earning-their-trust-for-the-greater-good.text: No problem.

the-mourners-plan.text: This is good news, give it a few days and the slave pens will be full again.

the-mourners-plan.player: So have I proved my commitment now?

the-mourners-plan.speaker: Essyllt
the-mourners-plan.text: Yes I think you have. I guess you want to know what we're doing in the mines?

the-mourners-plan.speaker: Essyllt
the-mourners-plan.text: A long time ago, Seren herself ordered the construction of a great temple deep beneath the earth. This temple guards a great power, one that is key to our plans.

the-mourners-plan.speaker: Essyllt
the-mourners-plan.text: We believe the temple lies beneath this city. That is why we are here.

the-mourners-plan.speaker: Essyllt
the-mourners-plan.text: Unfortunately, progress has been slower than we'd have liked. The slaves accidentally mined into some old caverns infested with beasts. They have caused us significant issues.

the-mourners-plan.player: I see. But how close are we to finding it?

the-mourners-plan.speaker: Essyllt
the-mourners-plan.text: It shouldn't be long now. We have started to see signs that we are near.

the-mourners-plan.speaker: Essyllt
the-mourners-plan.text: Anyway, now that you know about the temple, I have a new task for you to perform, deep within the mines.

the-mourners-plan.speaker: Essyllt
the-mourners-plan.text: Alas, one of the guards has taken the key to the mines to be copied. Report in regularly and I will see that you get a copy as soon as he gets back.

the-mourners-plan.speaker: Essyllt
the-mourners-plan.text: Now be on your way, I have other things to attend to.

the-mourners-plan.player: I should probably report this to Arianwyn.

the-mourners-plan-talking-to-essyllt-aga.player: Do you have the key to the mines yet?

the-mourners-plan-talking-to-essyllt-aga.speaker: Essyllt
the-mourners-plan-talking-to-essyllt-aga.text: No, the guard is being a bit slow, but we should have it soon.

the-mourners-plan-talking-to-essyllt-aga.player: Alright, I'll report in again later.

the-mourners-plan-talking-to-elena-again.speaker: Elena
the-mourners-plan-talking-to-elena-again.text: Hello [player name]. Have you found out what those mourners are up to yet?

the-mourners-plan-talking-to-elena-again.player: Apparently they are trying to find an old temple deep under the city. That's what their mining operation is for.
The temple seems to be the key to their plans. It apparently holds a great power. I still have no idea what that is yet though.

the-mourners-plan-talking-to-elena-again.speaker: Elena
the-mourners-plan-talking-to-elena-again.text: Well let me know when you find out.

the-mourners-plan-reporting-back-to-aria.player: I think I have the information you're after. It seems Iorwerth elves are searching for an ancient temple of some sort deep beneath West Ardougne.

the-mourners-plan-reporting-back-to-aria.speaker: Arianwyn
the-mourners-plan-reporting-back-to-aria.text: Temple? That must be the Temple of Light!

the-mourners-plan-reporting-back-to-aria.player: Temple of Light? What's the Temple of Light?

the-mourners-plan-reporting-back-to-aria.speaker: Arianwyn
the-mourners-plan-reporting-back-to-aria.text: It was built by Seren herself to guard a dark and ancient power. This is not good friend, I fear Lord Iorwerth intends to use that power to summon the Dark Lord!

the-mourners-plan-reporting-back-to-aria.player: I don't think they've found this temple yet, but they know it's down there.

the-mourners-plan-reporting-back-to-aria.speaker: Arianwyn
the-mourners-plan-reporting-back-to-aria.text: Well then we still have time. Thank you for your help so far, we would never have discovered this without you. Now we must prepare for what comes next.

the-mourners-plan-reporting-back-to-aria.player: So what are we going to do about the Temple of Light?

the-mourners-plan-reporting-back-to-aria.speaker: Arianwyn
the-mourners-plan-reporting-back-to-aria.text: First of all, we need to know how close the Iorwerth elves are to finding it. Do you think you are ready for this?

the-mourners-plan-reporting-back-to-aria.prompt: Start the Mourning's End Part II quest?

options.text: Yes.

steps.player: I'll head over there right away.

steps.speaker: Arianwyn
steps.text: Thank you friend. Don't forget your disguise.

options.text: No.

yvBLv1.player: Alright, I've managed to infiltrate the mourners. I just have to find out what they are up to now.

yvBLv1.speaker: Arianwyn
yvBLv1.text: Great work! Stick with it [player name].
